title: The beach clean-up
summary: Iker joins a beach clean-up to get school points and finds something more important.
paragraphs: Iker only went to the beach clean-up because his school gave extra points for {{volunteering}}. It was a Saturday morning in February, the wind was cold, and he had planned to stay in bed until twelve. Instead he was standing on the sand with a pair of gloves and a big plastic bag.

There were about thirty volunteers: retired people, families with small children, a group of surfers and a woman who organised everything with a loud voice and a {{clipboard}}. "Pick up everything that isn't sand, stones or shells," she said. "And write down what you find on this list. Scientists use the information."

At first Iker found the usual things: bottle tops, crisp packets, a flip-flop. But as he walked along the {{tide}} line, he started to notice how much there was. Tiny pieces of plastic were everywhere, mixed with the seaweed, too small to pick up one by one. A girl next to him held up a toothbrush. "Someone's toothbrush," she said, "on a beach where nobody lives."

In two hours, the group filled sixty bags. They also found a fishing net as big as a car, which took eight people to carry. The woman with the clipboard explained that nets like that are dangerous for {{turtles}} and dolphins, which get caught inside them. Iker looked at the net for a long time.

On Monday he told his class about it. He showed them the list of objects and the photos. His teacher asked him to prepare a short {{presentation}} for the whole school. Now Iker goes to the clean-up every month, even when there are no points. Last month he brought three friends. He still hates getting up early on Saturdays, but he says he hates finding toothbrushes on the beach even more.

volunteering.meaning: working for no money to help people or a cause

tide.meaning: the regular rising and falling of the sea

turtles.meaning: animals with a hard shell that live in the sea or on land

presentation.meaning: a talk in which you show information to a group

clipboard.meaning: a board with a clip that holds paper so you can write while standing
